story.title: Severe Wildfires Force Mass Evacuations in France and Spain
story.summary: Over 300,000 people have been evacuated from their homes in France and Spain due to severe wildfires that have been raging for several days. Fire crews are struggling to contain the unpredictable blazes, which have been exacerbated by an impending heatwave.

explore_lenses.label: How did conditions become so dangerous?
explore_lenses.title: Heat, dry fuels and wind compounded fire risk
explore_lenses.summary: The fires followed repeated hot and dry periods that left vegetation and soils unusually dry. Authorities and meteorological agencies also identified wind and low humidity as conditions that raise fire danger and complicate containment.

claims.text: Météo-France reported on July 22 that soil moisture across France was at an exceptionally low level for so early in summer, while hot, very dry and windy conditions kept fire danger high to very high across the south and west.
Météo-France recorded a 16-day French heatwave from July 4 to July 19, after an intense June heatwave; Bordeaux had nine very hot days from July 9 to July 17.
Spain’s Civil Protection said high temperatures, locally gusty southerly winds and widespread low humidity would push wildfire danger toward extreme levels.

explore_lenses.label: What could happen as the next heatwave arrives?
explore_lenses.title: Forecast heat may prolong the response
explore_lenses.summary: Conditions in some fire zones had shown signs of stabilizing, but official forecasts point to another period of intense heat. That raises the risk of renewed spread, new ignitions and a longer evacuation-and-suppression effort.

claims.text: Forecast: Météo-France said a new heat episode would begin on July 28, peak on July 29 and could bring temperatures up to 40°C in southwest France; its duration was still to be determined.
Forecast: Spain’s Civil Protection said the fourth heatwave of the summer was expected to start July 29 and last at least through August 2, with wildfire danger continuing to rise.
French officials reported the Gironde situation was stable overnight on July 27, but this was not equivalent to full containment and came before the forecast heat peak.

related_stories.title: Greta Thunberg Attends London Rally Supporting Indian Student Movement
related_stories.summary: Climate activist Greta Thunberg participated in a rally in London to support the Cockroach Janta Party-led student movement in India. The event celebrated recent successes of the movement, highlighting solidarity with the protesters.

related_stories.title: FIFA President Infantino Defends World Cup Amid Criticism
related_stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has responded to critics of the World Cup, accusing them of being 'consumed by hate' and spreading false narratives. In a strongly worded statement, he suggested that detractors should 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' instead of perpetuating negativity. Infantino defended the tournament as a celebration of unity, safety, and inclusion, dismissing concerns about corruption and disciplinary rulings.

related_stories.title: Oil Prices Decline as US and Iran Pause Strikes for Diplomatic Efforts
related_stories.summary: Oil prices fell on Monday following a pause in strikes between the US and Iran, which has raised hopes for renewed diplomatic talks. The US halted its attacks after 13 days, with officials indicating that this pause is intended to create 'space' for negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz.
